comments: Data representative of values reported in Table 2 of the paper:
Robert A. Emmons and Michael E. McCullough. Counting blessings versus burdens:
An experimental investigation of gratitude and subjective well-being in daily life.
Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 84(2):377–389, 2003.
In this study, undergraduate volunteers were randomly assigned to one of three groups.
Group 1 wrote down five things each week for which they were grateful.
Group 2 wrote down five hassles that occured in their lives.
Group 3 wrote down five things each week that had an impact on them.
The participants were asked to rate their feelings about life in general.
Higher scores indicate a more favorable disposition to life in general.
